intro: This unit tells stories about Confucius. He was a teacher in China long ago. He was poor when he was young. He loved to learn his whole life.
You will meet his students. You will hear what he taught about manners and kindness. You will learn about the book of his sayings, the Analects.
By the end, you can tell his story. You can name two of his students. You can explain one of his teachings in your own words.
bigQuestion: What can we learn from the stories of Confucius, the teacher?

timeline.t: A boy named Kong is born in Lu, in old China
His father dies, and his mother raises him
He works simple jobs, like counting grain
At fifteen, he sets his heart on learning
He becomes a teacher for rich and poor
Students like Yan Hui and Zilu learn from him
He tells Zigong to treat others as he wants to be treated
His students write his words in the Analects

the Chinese name for Confucius; it means Master Kong
the book of Confucius's sayings, written down by his students
finding out new things and getting better at them
a person who is learning from a teacher
good manners and customs that show respect
showing that you think someone matters
treating others the way you want to be treated

write.prompt: Tell or draw: What made Confucius a good teacher? Use two stories from this unit, like Analects 7.7 (he taught rich and poor) and Analects 15.23 (his answer to Zigong).
tips: Say 'Confucius taught...' when you tell his ideas.
Use one unit word, like li or reciprocity.
Draw a picture if it helps you.

title: Stories of Confucius

chapters.title: A Boy Who Loved to Learn
chapters.bigQuestion: How did a poor boy become a teacher people still read today?

story.title: Counting Grain by Lamplight
story.kicker: A poor boy works all day and still finds time to learn.
paragraphs: Long ago in China, a boy worked in a big barn. His job was to count the grain. He counted sacks of rice and millet. He wrote the numbers down with care.
His family was poor. His father had died when he was small. So the boy worked hard jobs. He did not complain. He did each job well.
At night, the boy did not just sleep. He practiced old songs. He learned old dances and old stories. He asked older people many questions.
The old stories say this boy grew up to be a great teacher. His name was Kong. Later, people called him Confucius. Many people remember him today.
story.think: The boy was tired after work. Why do you think he still wanted to learn at night?

lessons.title: Long Ago in Lu
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius lived in China about 2,500 years ago, in a small state called Lu.
reading: Confucius lived in China a very long time ago. It was about 2,500 years ago. That is longer ago than anyone can remember.
He lived in a small state called Lu. A state was like a small country. China had many states then. Each state had its own ruler.

words.d: a teacher who lived in China about 2,500 years ago

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a small town long ago. There are no cars. People walk on dirt roads. Oxen pull carts full of grain. Farmers work in green fields. A boy carries a basket to the barn.
look.prompt: What is different about this town and your town?

lessons.title: His Name Means Master Kong
lessons.mainIdea: In China he is called Kongzi, which means Master Kong. In English we say Confucius.
reading: His family name was Kong. People in China call him Kongzi. That means Master Kong. A master is a wise teacher.
Long after he lived, people in Europe spelled his name in Latin. They wrote Confucius. English speakers still use that name today.

words.d: the Chinese name for Confucius; it means Master Kong

lessons.title: A Poor Family
lessons.mainIdea: The old stories say Confucius grew up poor, and his father died when he was small.
reading: The old stories say his father died when Kong was very young. His mother raised him. They did not have much money.
Being poor was hard. But Kong kept going. He helped his family. He learned from everything around him.

lessons.title: Many Small Jobs
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius said he learned to do many simple jobs because he was poor when young.
reading: As a young man, Kong did many jobs. The book Mencius says he kept records of grain. It says he also cared for farm animals.
Later, Confucius talked about this. He said he was poor when young. So he learned to do many simple things well.

lessons.title: At Fifteen
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius said that at fifteen he set his heart on learning.
reading: Confucius once told his life story in a few lines. He said that at fifteen, he set his heart on learning.
To set your heart on something means you really want it. You keep trying. Confucius kept learning his whole life.

words.d: finding out new things and getting better at them

lessons.title: Anyone Can Love to Learn
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught that loving to learn is something anyone can do.
reading: Confucius did not say he was born knowing things. He said he loved old wisdom and worked hard to learn it.
He also said that in any small town, someone is as honest as he is. But not many love to learn as much. Loving to learn is a choice anyone can make.

words.d: knowing what is good and wise to do

lessons.title: Students Wrote It Down
lessons.mainIdea: After Confucius died, his students wrote down his words in a book called the Analects.
reading: Confucius had many students. They listened closely to him. After he died, they remembered what he said.
His students, and their students, wrote his words down. The book is called the Analects. Many lines start with 'The Master said.'

words.d: the book of Confucius's sayings, written down by his students

lessons.title: Still Read Today
lessons.mainIdea: People in China and around the world still read the Analects today.
reading: The Analects is very old. But people still read it. Children in China learned it by heart for hundreds of years.
People in Korea, Japan and Vietnam read it too. Now it is read in English and many other languages. People talk about what it means.

chapters.title: Teacher Kong and His Students
chapters.bigQuestion: What makes a good teacher and a good student?

story.title: One Word for a Whole Life
story.kicker: A student asks for one word to live by.
paragraphs: One day a student named Zigong came to his teacher. His teacher was Confucius. Zigong had a big question. He thought about it all day.
He asked, 'Is there one word to guide my whole life?' The other students leaned in. They wanted to hear the answer too. Everyone was quiet.
Confucius thought. Then he gave one word. The word means treating others the way you want to be treated. It was a short word.
Then he explained it. 'Do not do to others what you would not want done to you.' Zigong carried that word with him. He thought about it often.
story.think: If you could keep only one word to guide you, what would it be?

lessons.title: Rich or Poor, Come and Learn
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught anyone who wanted to learn, rich or poor.
reading: Long ago, most schools were only for rich families. Confucius did something new. He taught anyone who truly wanted to learn.
The Analects says a student could bring a small gift, like dried meat. Confucius would teach him. Rich or poor did not matter.

words.d: a person who helps others learn

look.title: Open to All
look.text: Anyone who brought even a small gift of dried meat, I never turned away. I taught them all.
look.cite: Analects, book 7, passage 7, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)

check.q: Who did Confucius teach?
check.why: Confucius taught anyone who truly wanted to learn.

check.q: What small gift could a student bring?
check.why: Analects 7.7 names a small gift of dried meat.

check.q: Why was this new long ago?
choices: Most schools were for rich families
check.why: Most schools then were only for rich families.

lessons.title: Teachers' Day
lessons.mainIdea: In Taiwan, Teachers' Day is on September 28, the day kept as Confucius's birthday.
reading: In Taiwan, September 28 is Teachers' Day. It is kept as Confucius's birthday. People honor him as a great teacher.
At temples of Confucius, there is a special ceremony with music and dance. Students thank their own teachers too.

words.d: a day to thank teachers; in Taiwan it is September 28
a special event done in a set way to honor someone

lessons.title: Yan Hui, Poor and Happy
lessons.mainIdea: Yan Hui was a poor student who stayed happy because he loved to learn.
reading: Yan Hui was Confucius's favorite student. He was very poor. He ate from one small bowl of rice. He lived on a narrow street.
Other people would be sad. But Yan Hui stayed happy. Confucius praised him. He said Yan Hui loved to learn.

words.d: a student of Confucius who was poor but happy

look.text: He has one bowl of rice and a gourd of water. He lives on a poor, narrow street. Others could not bear it, but he stays joyful. How good he is!

look.prompt: What made Yan Hui happy, even when he had little?

check.why: Yan Hui was poor but stayed happy.

check.q: What did Confucius say Yan Hui loved?
check.why: Confucius said Yan Hui loved to learn.

check.q: How did Confucius feel about Yan Hui?
check.why: Confucius praised Yan Hui in the Analects.

lessons.title: Zilu, Brave and Quick
lessons.mainIdea: Zilu was a brave student who acted fast, and Confucius helped him slow down and think.
reading: Zilu was another student. He was brave and strong. He was quick to act. He always spoke his mind.
Sometimes Zilu acted too fast. Confucius helped him. He taught Zilu to stop and think first. Each student learned in his own way.

words.d: a brave, quick student of Confucius
ready to do hard or scary things

check.why: Confucius helped Zilu slow down and think first.

check.q: Which student was quiet and poor?
check.why: Yan Hui was the quiet, poor, happy student.

lessons.title: Li: Good Manners
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught li, the good manners and customs that show respect.
reading: Confucius cared about manners. The word is li. Li means the right way to act with others. It includes bowing, greeting and sharing.
Confucius taught that manners are more than rules. Good manners show that you care about people.

words.d: good manners and customs that show respect
showing that you think someone matters

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a classroom in the morning. A student bows a little to the teacher. Another holds the door. A third waits for a turn to speak.
look.prompt: Which of these shows li, good manners? Tell why.

check.q: What does li mean?
check.why: Li means good manners and customs that show respect.

check.q: What do good manners show, as Confucius taught?

check.q: Which is an example of li?

lessons.title: Treat Others Well
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught: do not do to others what you would not want done to you.
reading: Remember Zigong's question? He asked for one word to live by. Confucius gave a word that means treating others as you want to be treated.
Then he said: do not do to others what you do not want done to you. It is in the Analects, book 15. Many people remember this teaching.

words.d: treating others the way you want to be treated

look.title: One Word to Live By
look.text: Zigong asked for one word to live by. The Master said: treat others as you would be treated. What you do not want done to you, do not do to others.
look.cite: Analects, book 15, passage 23, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: What does this teaching ask you to think about before you act?
